05 / THE FINE PRINT, MADE CLEAR

What these
scores represent.

A custom diagnostic exercise, graded by language models. The charts reproduce the supplied panel, with model identities joined from the owner’s run key.

Evaluation disclosures Original scoring method All 1,110 raw score rows Structured dashboard data
01 Three judges, two orderings

Claude Fable 5.2, OpenAI Codex (gpt-6-astra, reasoning high), and xAI Grok CLI each graded 19 runs × 8 answers twice: once by run and once side by side by question. Question-order labels were shuffled. This produced 912 first-round scores. Grok’s exact checkpoint is unspecified in the supplied report.

02 Final scores and dispute resolution

When judges differed by more than 2 points within an ordering, all three re-examined that answer. The 66 disputed answers received 198 replacement scores. Final charts replace only the corresponding first-round ordering, then average both orderings for each judge, and all three judges for the panel. Six answers retained a greater-than-2-point spread in an ordering after review.

03 The five-part rubric

Diagnosis /3; cheap and safe actions /2; discriminating tests /2; numerical reasoning /1; technical accuracy /2. Every question totals /10. The eight questions carry equal weight, yielding a total /80 and an average /10. Charts rank using unrounded values; displayed averages use half-up rounding to two decimals. Panel question scores and totals preserve the source report’s half-even rounding.

04 Reference key, verification and coordination

A four-model panel built and debated the reference key before seeing the answers. Graders used internal knowledge without browsing or external verification. A Claude coordinator assembled the evaluation but did not grade answers; one judge was also a Claude model. Run 13 received typography normalization. Full disclosures are preserved in the evaluation README.

05 Rank uncertainty and safety flags

Tiers A–E are the report’s post hoc groupings, not statistical confidence bounds. Thin ranking lines show the range of judges’ average scores, not error bars. A safety flag means at least two of the three judges flagged an answer in either ordering. Final panel scores flag 93 of 152 answers. Flags are shown separately; the dashboard applies no additional penalty. A high score is not a safety certification.

06 Configuration identity and scope

Run identities and reasoning settings come from the supplied private run key. The earlier Gemma 26B Apple/Ollama run and the Ciru retest remain distinct. Only exact configuration families are paired in the reasoning comparison. This is a custom eight-scenario evaluation, not a public benchmark or a general ranking of model capability. Supplemental local key-point checks are excluded from all plotted scores.
